claim: The Legislature convenes in regular session on the first Monday in December of each even-numbered year and adjourns at midnight on November 30 two years later
quote: The Legislature shall convene in regular session at noon on the first Monday in December of each even-numbered year

claim: In the first year of the session, the governor has 30 days after the joint recess to act on bills in their possession
quote: that is not returned within 30 days after that date becomes a statute

claim: In the second year, bills passed before September 1 and held by the governor become law unless returned by September 30
quote: that is not returned on or before September 30 of that year becomes a statute

claim: A regular-session statute takes effect on January 1 after a 90-day period from enactment
quote: a statute enacted at a regular session shall go into effect on January 1 next following a 90-day period from the date of enactment of the statute

claim: All judicial, school, county and city offices are nonpartisan
quote: All judicial, school, county, and city offices, including the Superintendent of Public Instruction, shall be nonpartisan.

claim: Parties may not nominate for nonpartisan office and the candidate's party preference is not on the ballot
quote: the candidate's party preference shall not be included on the ballot for the nonpartisan office

claim: The Elections Code defines judicial, school, county and municipal offices as nonpartisan
quote: Judicial, school, county, and municipal offices, including the Superintendent of Public Instruction, are nonpartisan offices.

claim: Congressional and state offices use a voter-nominated (top-two) primary open to all voters
quote: The candidates who are the top two vote-getters at a voter-nominated primary election for a congressional or state elective office shall, regardless of party preference, compete in the ensuing general election.

claim: Any voter may vote for any candidate at a top-two primary regardless of party preference
quote: any qualified voter may vote for any candidate for a voter-nominated office

claim: Top-two candidates show "Party Preference: None" if they declined to disclose a party
quote: Party Preference: None

claim: Voter-nominated offices list (Governor through Assembly)
quote: serves to winnow the candidates for the general election to the candidates receiving the highest or second highest number of votes cast at the primary election

claim: Presidential and party committee primaries remain partisan
quote: The Legislature shall provide for partisan elections for presidential candidates, and political party and party central committees

claim: A voter with no party preference gets a nonpartisan ballot at a partisan primary unless they ask for a party ballot the party allows
quote: each voter not registered disclosing a preference for any one of the political parties participating in the election shall be furnished only a nonpartisan ballot, unless the voter requests a ballot of a political party

claim: Voters may decline to disclose a party preference when registering
quote: an elector may decline to disclose a political party preference

claim: American Independent Party is a political party in California (a party, not a lack of one)
citation: Secretary of State, Qualified Political Parties
quote: American Independent Party

claim: Established election dates
quote: The first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each year.

claim: All state, county, municipal, district and school district elections must be on an established election date
quote: all state, county, municipal, district, and school district elections shall be held on an established election date

claim: Election date rules do not bind charter cities and charter counties whose charters differ, or recall/initiative elections
quote: Elections held in chartered cities or chartered counties in which the charter provisions are inconsistent with this chapter.

claim: Statewide general election is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even years
quote: The statewide general election shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each even-numbered year.

claim: Statewide primary: June in gubernatorial years, March in presidential years
quote: The statewide direct primary shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in June of each even-numbered year that is not evenly divisible by four and on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in March in each even-numbered year that is evenly divisible by four.

claim: District attorney and sheriff are elected at the presidential primary
quote: An election to select a district attorney and sheriff shall be held with the presidential primary.

claim: Other county officers are elected at the gubernatorial primary, with a November runoff if no one wins outright
quote: an election to select county officers other than district attorney and sheriff shall be held with the statewide primary at which candidates for Governor are nominated

claim: A board of supervisors may move other county offices (except county superintendent) to the presidential primary
quote: a county board of supervisors may adopt an ordinance to hold an election to select any county officer other than a county superintendent of schools with the presidential primary

claim: A general municipal election is on an established election date; a city council may move it by ordinance with the supervisors' approval
quote: a city council may enact an ordinance, pursuant to Division 10 (commencing with Section 10000), requiring its general municipal election to be held on the day of the statewide direct primary election, the day of the statewide general election

claim: The ordinance takes effect on approval by the board of supervisors
quote: An ordinance adopted pursuant to this subdivision shall become operative upon approval by the county board of supervisors.

claim: Moving a city election date cannot lengthen or shorten a term by more than 12 months
quote: no term of office shall be increased or decreased by more than 12 months

claim: School, community college and county board of education elections default to November of odd years, and may move to a statewide or municipal election date by resolution
quote: shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each odd-numbered year

claim: The school board resolution becomes operative on supervisors' approval
quote: The resolution shall become operative upon approval by the board of supervisors pursuant to Section 10404.5 or 10405.7, as applicable.

claim: Special district elections default to November of odd years; a district may move to the statewide general election
quote: a governing body of a special district may require, by resolution, that its elections of governing body members be held on the same day as the statewide general election

claim: Special district default date
quote: on the first Tuesday following the first Monday in November of each odd-numbered year

claim: A political subdivision may not hold an off-cycle election if that has caused a significant turnout drop
quote: a political subdivision shall not hold an election other than on a statewide election date if holding an election on a nonconcurrent date has previously resulted in a significant decrease in voter turnout

claim: Significant decrease means at least 25 percent below the average of the previous four statewide general elections
quote: at least 25 percent less than the average voter turnout within that political subdivision for the previous four statewide general elections

claim: Political subdivision includes cities, school districts, community college districts and other districts
quote: including, but not limited to, a city, a school district, a community college district, or other district organized pursuant to state law

claim: The turnout rule has applied since 1 January 2018
quote: This chapter shall become operative on January 1, 2018.

claim: A nonpartisan candidate with a majority at the primary is elected outright
quote: Any candidate for a nonpartisan office who at a primary election receives votes on a majority of all the ballots cast for candidates for that office shall be elected to that office.

claim: Otherwise the top vote-getters, twice the number of seats, go to the general election
quote: equal in number to twice the number remaining to be elected to that office

claim: Plurality wins unless a charter, city law or the county primary runoff rule says otherwise
quote: The person who receives a plurality of the votes cast for any office is elected or nominated to that office in any election, except: (a) An election for which different provision is made by any city or county charter.

claim: Nomination papers: signers must be voters in the jurisdiction
quote: Signers shall be voters in the district or political subdivision in which the candidate is to be voted on.

claim: A signer may not sign for more candidates than there are seats
quote: I have not signed more nomination papers than there are places to be filled in the above-named office

claim: City candidates are nominated by voters signing a nomination paper; no voter may sign more than one for the same office
quote: No voter may sign more than one nomination paper for the same office

claim: Candidate must file a declaration of candidacy and nomination papers
quote: Nomination papers signed by signers pursuant to Section 8041.

claim: Independent nomination after the primary is open to nonpartisan offices only when no one was nominated or elected at the primary
quote: A candidate for nonpartisan office or for voter-nominated office may be nominated subsequent to, or by other means than, a primary election pursuant to this chapter only if a candidate was not nominated or elected at the primary election for that office.

claim: Uniform District Election Law governs special district elections
quote: This part may be cited as the Uniform District Election Law.

claim: Some special districts are landowner-voting districts
quote: “Landowner voting district” means a district whose principal act requires an elector to be an owner of land located within the district.

claim: State divided into counties
quote: The State is divided into counties which are legal subdivisions of the State.

claim: Every county has an elected sheriff, district attorney, assessor and governing body
quote: an elected county sheriff, an elected district attorney, an elected assessor, and an elected governing body in each county

claim: A general law county has a five-member board of supervisors on staggered four-year terms
quote: Each county shall have a board of supervisors consisting of five members.

claim: Supervisor terms are four years
quote: Thereafter the term of office of each member shall be four years.

claim: Supervisors are elected by district
quote: Each member of the board of supervisors shall be elected by the district which he represents, and not at large

claim: Elected county officers by default
quote: the county officers to be elected by the people are the treasurer, county clerk, auditor, sheriff, tax collector, district attorney, recorder, assessor, public administrator, and coroner

claim: County voters may make an elective office appointive, except sheriff, DA and assessor
quote: any county office that is required to be elective may become an appointive office pursuant to this subdivision

claim: Supervisors may consolidate county offices (e.g. clerk-recorder, treasurer-tax collector, sheriff-coroner)
quote: By ordinance the board of supervisors may consolidate the duties of certain of the county offices in one or more of these combinations

claim: Combination list includes sheriff and coroner, treasurer and tax collector, clerk and recorder
quote: (n) Sheriff and coroner.

claim: Any county or city may adopt a charter by majority vote
quote: For its own government, a county or city may adopt a charter by majority vote of its electors voting on the question.

claim: County charters must provide a governing body of 5 or more and an elected sheriff, DA and assessor
quote: A governing body of 5 or more members, elected (1) by district or, (2) at large, or (3) at large, with a requirement that they reside in a district.

claim: County charters set terms of the governing body and the election or appointment of other officers
quote: An elected sheriff, an elected district attorney, an elected assessor, other officers, their election or appointment, compensation, terms and removal.

claim: City charters may provide for the conduct of city elections and the times and terms of municipal officers
quote: (3) conduct of city elections

claim: Charter city plenary authority over manner, method, times and terms of elected officers
quote: the manner in which, the method by which, the times at which, and the terms for which the several municipal officers and employees whose compensation is paid by the city shall be elected or appointed

claim: A county and its cities may consolidate as a charter city and county
quote: A county and all cities within it may consolidate as a charter city and county as provided by statute.

claim: A charter city and county is both; city powers prevail
quote: A charter city and county is a charter city and a charter county. Its charter city powers supersede conflicting charter county powers.

claim: Cities are either chartered cities or general law cities
quote: Cities organized under the general law shall be “general law cities.”

claim: Chartered cities defined
quote: Cities organized under a charter shall be “chartered cities.”

claim: Any city or city and county may enact a charter
quote: Any city or city and county may enact, amend, or repeal a charter for its own government

claim: "Town" is only a name: a council can swap "city" and "town" in the corporate name
quote: eliminate the word “city” from the corporate name and substitute the word “town”

claim: A general law city has a council of at least five, a city clerk and a city treasurer
quote: A city council of at least five members. (b) A city clerk. (c) A city treasurer.

claim: Voters may make the clerk and treasurer appointive
quote: the city council may submit to the electors the question whether the elective officers, or any of them except council members, shall be appointed by the city council

claim: By default the council chooses one of its members as mayor
quote: choose one of its number as mayor, and one of its number as mayor pro tempore

claim: Voters may choose to elect a mayor directly, for a two- or four-year term
quote: whether electors shall thereafter elect a mayor and four city council members, and whether the mayor shall serve a two-year or four-year term

claim: An elected mayor is a member of the council
quote: The mayor is a member of the city council and has all of the powers and duties of a member of the city council.

claim: By-district councils may have five, seven or nine districts
quote: By districts in five, seven, or nine districts.

claim: District council terms are four years unless otherwise provided
quote: shall be four years, unless otherwise expressly provided

claim: A council may switch to district elections by ordinance without a vote, citing the Voting Rights Act
quote: without being required to submit the ordinance to the voters for approval

claim: Councils or voters may set term limits for council members and elected mayors
quote: a proposal to limit or repeal a limit on the number of terms a member of the city council may serve on the city council

claim: Default school board: five members elected at large to staggered four-year terms
quote: the governing board of a school district shall consist of five regular members elected at large by the qualified voters of the school district

claim: Unified districts may have seven members
quote: A unified school district may have a governing board of seven regular members

claim: Small districts may cut boards to three; county committee may move between five and seven
quote: may decrease from five to three the number of members of the governing board

claim: School board term is four years
quote: shall hold office for a term of four years

claim: Community college boards of five or seven, four-year terms
quote: there shall be a governing board of either five or seven members elected at large from the district to serve a term of four years

claim: Every county except a city and county has an elected county board of education of five or seven members by trustee area; charter counties may differ
quote: Except in a city and county, there shall be a county board of education

claim: In charter counties, the charter or supervisors decide how the county board of education is chosen
quote: In chartered counties, the manner of selection of the county board of education shall be prescribed in the county charter, or by the county board of supervisors.

claim: County superintendent of schools may be elected or appointed, as county voters decide
quote: may be elected by the qualified electors thereof at each gubernatorial election or may be appointed by the county board of education

claim: City charters may set how boards of education are elected or appointed
quote: the manner in which, the times at which, and the terms for which the members of boards of education shall be elected or appointed

claim: School and community college districts may elect by trustee area instead of at large
quote: That one or more members residing in each trustee area be elected by the registered voters of that particular trustee area.

claim: The 2026 amendments to the California Voting Rights Act (SB 1164, Stats. 2026, ch. 338) change how district remedies are ordered and do not amend the sections cited here
Cities are the general-purpose local government below counties; the Legislature provides for city formation and powers
quote: The Legislature shall prescribe uniform procedure for city formation and provide for city powers.
